Chapter 9—Adapting to Change: Resilience and Flexibility.
Change—it's always knocking at our door, especially at work. New tech, shifting priorities, maybe a curveball or two... they all ask us to adapt, sometimes quicker than we'd like.
So, what does it really mean to be resilient? Well, think of it as bending without breaking. It's about bouncing back from stress and keeping your momentum, even when things get tough.
But here's the thing: our brains aren’t exactly thrilled about change. Uncertainty? That tends to trigger our threat response. Suddenly, it’s tougher to think outside the box or even stay focused.
The good news? With some practice, you can actually train your mind to be more flexible.
Want to build resilience? Let’s break it down:
First, try reframing challenges. Instead of seeing them as threats, what if you viewed them as opportunities to learn? That little shift can make all the difference.
Next, don’t tackle everything at once. Break big changes into smaller, more manageable steps. That way, you’re not overwhelming your brain—and you’re more likely to follow through.
And don’t forget the power of support. Talk things out with others. Share your concerns, brainstorm solutions together. Sometimes, just knowing you're not alone can lighten the load.
Flexibility is part of the equation too. Say a project you’ve been preparing for suddenly gets delayed. Instead of getting stuck in frustration, try channeling your energy into a different, meaningful task. It keeps you moving—and keeps your spirits up.
Being resilient doesn't mean you never feel stress. It just means you bounce back faster. And a big part of that? Self-compassion. When you hit a setback, treat yourself with kindness, not criticism. Your brain actually responds to your own encouragement, just like it does to support from a friend.
In teams, resilience is kind of contagious. When leaders show adaptability and optimism, others usually follow. Rituals help too—like debriefing after a tough week, or celebrating the small wins. Little moments like these help teams stick together when things get rough.
So, if you remember one thing, let it be this: resilience is about staying grounded in the middle of change. It’s using your inner strengths, and leaning on your community, to find your way through the unknown.
